note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a CAM 24, 25; A06b CAM 24, 25; L05 CAM 31(a)): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Wedlock restriction), A01b (descent, born abroad: Wedlock restriction), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: Generally applicable provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory only on the condition the dataset states; by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. The coding also records a wedlock restriction (a child born out of wedlock may not take it from a citizen father), which the form doesn't hold. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Cameroon, 2024

Person is born in Cameroon in wedlock and either parent is a citizen. ... Wedlock restriction ... Person is born abroad in wedlock and either parent is a citizen. ... No provision ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Cameroon of one parent who was also born there.
